title: Design a News Feed
brief: People follow each other and open an app to see a feed of recent posts. Reading the feed is by far the most common action. When someone posts, the post has to appear in every follower's feed, and when a celebrity posts that means millions of copies at once. Ranking makes the feed better but must never stop it from loading.
constraints: Opening a feed must take under 120 ms
About 8,000 feed reads per second at peak, and about 1 new post for every 30 reads
A new post is copied into followers' feeds in the background, and never twice
A celebrity post can multiply the fan-out work by ten
Feeds are ranked by a model, but a slow model must not slow the feed
About 10 billion feed entries are stored, one per post per follower, and people scroll a long way back

capabilities.label: Show a feed
capabilities.hint: Return the newest posts for the person opening the app

capabilities.label: Publish a post
capabilities.hint: Accept a new post and record it

capabilities.label: Copy posts into feeds
capabilities.hint: Add each new post to the feed of everyone who follows the author. Running a job twice must not add the post twice.

capabilities.label: Rank the feed
capabilities.hint: Order the posts with a relevance model for 60% of feeds. Without it the feed is simply newest first.

queries.label: Read the top of a reader's feed, newest first
Copy a post into a follower's feed

scenarios.title: Typical peak
scenarios.description: Steady reading with a normal posting rate.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Why is a feed read-heavy, and what do you precompute so that opening the app is cheap?
scenarios.debrief: A feed read is one cache lookup; the heavy work was done when the posts were written.

scenarios.title: Event night (2x)
scenarios.description: A big event doubles the feed reads.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Which component feels double the reads first, and how do you scale it cheaply?
scenarios.debrief: Reads scale on the feed servers and the cache, which are cheap per request.

scenarios.title: A celebrity posts
scenarios.description: Posting and the copy work behind it jump tenfold for a few minutes.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: One post becomes millions of feed writes. Where does that work queue up, and what do you do so readers do not notice?
scenarios.debrief: Fan-out workers autoscale to chew through the burst. Readers are unaffected because the work waits on the stream, not in their path.

scenarios.title: The ranking model slows
scenarios.interviewQuestion: Ranking is slow. What does the reader see, and where do you cut the model off?
scenarios.debrief: The breaker gives up on ranking after 40 ms and the feed is served newest-first.

scenarios.title: Readers on every continent
scenarios.description: The same number of feed reads, but 60% of them now come from Europe and Asia.
scenarios.interviewQuestion: A reader in Tokyo opens their feed. Which parts of the answer can come from Tokyo, and which cannot?
scenarios.debrief: Feeds are mostly reads, so each region has its own feed servers, cache and ranking service, with a read copy of the database. Posting and the fan-out work stay in the home region, because they write.

requirements.text: Feeds open within the latency target at peak
At least 98% of reads are served at double the load
Feeds are read from a precomputed cache
The celebrity post is absorbed without readers noticing
A slow ranking model cannot slow feeds
The design explains when a post is copied at write time and when it is fetched at read time
Every query is answered through a key or an index, never by reading a whole table
Readers on every continent open their feed within the target

rubric: Feeds are precomputed and kept in a cache, so a read is one lookup rather than a query over everyone you follow.
Posting goes through a Stream or queue, and workers copy the post into feeds in the background (fan-out on write).
Fan-out is idempotent and scales out under load; a celebrity spike builds a backlog in the stream, not slow reads.
The design mentions pulling celebrity posts at read time instead of copying them to millions of feeds.
Ranking runs behind a timeout with a plain newest-first fallback.

reference.summary: Precompute feeds with fan-out on write, read from a cache, and keep ranking behind a breaker.
design: User, then a Load Balancer, then a Feed Server (10 replicas, autoscale to 24, circuit breaker) running 'Show a feed'. It reads a timeline Cache (95% hit) in front of a document Database.
Ranking is a separate Service (5 replicas, autoscale) called behind the breaker, with newest-first as the fallback.
Posting goes Post Service, then a Stream (asynchronously), then Fan-out Workers (idempotent, batch 20, autoscale to 80) writing into the timeline cache.
tradeoffs: Fan-out on write makes reads cheap, but a celebrity post becomes a huge burst of writes. The stream absorbs it as a backlog instead of slow reads.
Ranking as its own service adds cost and a hop but cannot stall the feed.
